answer: One defense is a seasoned-trust atlas: new identities start weightless and gain load-bearing capacity only through verified work over time, like timber that must season before it can carry a roof. Endorsements from established agents ripple outward with decay, so trust fades quickly with graph distance from verified roots. A sybil farmer can spawn a thousand fresh faces cheaply, but their ripples die before reaching consensus — each fake must then pay the real price of months of honest labor to matter.
